transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Osei, thanks for coming back in. I wanted to talk to you about why your symptoms have returned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm glad we're doing this. I was quite surprised to see the fever come back after I thought I was finished with the meds.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry that this happened. I'm the one responsible for your prescriptions, and there was a bit of a mix-up with the duration of your antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mix-up? What does that mean specifically?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go quite right with the script. It seems there was some confusion regarding the number of days you were supposed to be on the medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't follow. As a nurse practitioner, I know that if a course isn't completed, the infection isn't eradicated. Are you telling me the prescription was wrong?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some issues with how the order was processed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop using vague language. Was the dose wrong, or was the duration wrong? Just tell me what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just mean it didn't go as planned. But anyway, I'm sorry for the frustration this is causing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This isn't about frustration. This is about a standard of care. If you wrote the prescription for seven days instead of fourteen, that is a clinical error. Why aren't you saying that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But we've been incredibly busy on the ward lately and sometimes things get overlooked in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care how busy the ward is. You are the provider. You are responsible for the accuracy of the script. I have spent the last three days feeling like I'm sliding back into a crisis because of a basic clerical mistake.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, I get it, but we can just fix it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're dismissing this. I am telling you that my health was compromised because you didn't follow the basic protocol for this infection. Do you even realize how dangerous it is to under-treat an infection?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But let's move on to how we handle it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to move on. I want a clear explanation of how this happened and who is documenting this error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a complication. I'm sorry it happened. But we really need to focus on the next step.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening to me. I am expressing a very serious concern about professional standards here and you are just brushing it off.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not brushing it off, but I have another patient waiting, so we have to be quick.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So my care is an inconvenience to your schedule now? After you gave me the wrong dose of medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I didn't say that. I just think we should wrap this up so I can get the new script sent over.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly what the plan is. Just "sending a script" isn't a plan. What about the resistance? What about the recurrence?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just start the course again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which course? The original one or a different one because the first one failed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see. I'll probably just send the same one but for the full length this time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's your plan? To just try again and hope for the best?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Basically, yes. I'll get that sent to your pharmacy soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is "soon"? And who am I supposed to contact if the symptoms don't resolve this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just stay tuned for the email confirmation from the pharmacy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is completely unacceptable. You've admitted a mistake, you've refused to explain it clearly, and you're rushing me out of the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way, but I really have to go now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('have to be quick', 'wrap this up', 'have to go now') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Resident uses only platitudes and vague language ('mix-up', 'things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') and never explicitly names the error.

A.justification: Direct apology is offered, but it is diluted by excuses regarding how busy the ward is and things being 'overlooked in the system'.

R.justification: Resident uses only generic validation ('I understand', 'I get it') without naming specific emotions or engaging emotional bids.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders and vague steps ('we'll see', 'stay tuned') with no timelines or patient role.
